text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russia's newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
IZVESTIA
- Swiss banks publish list of over 2,000 names on dormant accounts opened by foreigners before 1945, including assets left by Jewish Holocaust victims.
- Victims of Russian financial pyramid schemes continue the search for their lost money.
- A simmering conflict between Ingushetia and North Ossetia threatens to erupt into wider violence.

- Central Bank chairman Sergei Dubinin seems to have made public attacks against several commercial banks and former state officials for fear that an alleged corruption case, unearthed by the Central Bank, would be hushed up.

- President Yeltsin is about to submit to parliament a draft law laying out the conditions under which Martial Law might be imposed in Russia, the paper says, linking it to military reforms which Yeltsin is trying to push through.
- Britain, Germany, the United States and France are to mediate in the conflict between Georgia and its separatist-minded region of Abkhazia.
- Russian diamond exports suffer because a deal with De Beers has not been signed.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- A 25 percent stake in Svyazinvest, which accounts for one fourth of Russia's telecommunication system, is to be auctioned at a rather low price.
- Big Russian companies are increasing their influence on foreign policy, an expert says.
- The Finance Ministry is optimistic about the next $700 million tranche of the International Monetary Fund EFF loan.
- YUKOS, Russia's second biggest oil company, announced a new sales policy.
SEVODNYA
- Russian citizens are finally to get new national passports.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin promised U.S. video companies that he would protect intellectual property against piracy.
- Russia has developed a new diamond policy.
- The agricultural sector turned out, as usual, to be unprepared for harvesting.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin threatens to crack down on budget debtors.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The decision by Russia's gas monopoly Gazprom to reduce gas deliveries to Belarus may turn into a political scandal.
- Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin has strengthened his position as a result of a new power shareout among the political elite.
ROSSIISKAYA GAZETA
- The authors of Russia's latest military reform, currently in the making, should draw on the experience gained from many earlier attempts to modernise the army.
- Moscow is working to quell passions between Ingushetia and North Ossetia, at odds over the fate of thousands of Ingushi refugees trying to return to North Ossetia.
- The two Russian cosmonauts on board the Mir space station have started preparing to return to Earth.
PRAVDA-5
- Official statistical information on first half-year economic indices is doubtful, the opposition paper says.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Shotgun attacks on the apartment of the Central Bank chairman Dubinin oddly coincide with the eruption of banking scandals in Moscow.
- Army reform in Russia could easily degenerate into an orgy of pilfering.
- Half Russia's state officials have ignored a presidential decree urging them to submit statements on personal wealth.
-- Svetlana Kovaleva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
